sessionTitle: Using autonomous SRE to move from alerts to action

announcements.name: Azure SRE Agent for incident management and resource optimization
announcements.shortDescription: An always-on AI teammate that automates operational tasks, accelerates root cause analysis, and is fully customizable to an organization's standards
announcements.longDescription: Azure SRE Agent is an AI-powered agent for incident management and resource optimization in production environments. It offers three core value propositions: automating operational tasks to keep applications running and protect revenue, accelerating root cause analysis to improve reliability and availability, and being fully customizable to an enterprise's unique operational needs and standards. Described as an always-on SRE teammate that learns how your environment works and acts according to how you want it to, it helped Ecolab reduce daily alerts for site reliability engineers from 30-40 a day down to under 10 a day.

announcements.name: CLI-based agent creation and management
announcements.shortDescription: Developers can create, configure, and interact with the SRE Agent entirely from developer tools like the terminal and Copilot CLI, using prebuilt recipes from the Microsoft SRE Agent repo rather than the Azure Portal
announcements.longDescription: Instead of going to the Azure Portal, developers can create, configure, and interact with the SRE Agent completely from their developer tools such as the Terminal and Copilot CLI. To create a new agent, you can use one of the prebuilt recipes hosted in the Microsoft SRE Agent repo, which come with a set of connectors, tools, and skills available out of the box so you don't have to build from scratch. The recipe shown creates an agent that connects to GitHub and Dynatrace and is customized to understand the architecture of hosted applications like App Service and PostgreSQL.

announcements.name: SRE Agent endpoint as an MCP server
announcements.shortDescription: The agent can be accessed as an MCP server to view analyses or configure it outside the Azure Portal
announcements.longDescription: The SRE Agent endpoint can be accessed as an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server, allowing developers to connect to it to either view the analysis the agent performed or configure things outside of the Azure Portal. The presenter uses Copilot CLI with a locally running MCP to connect to the newly created agent, checking the JSON configuration file and applying the deployment URL. This capability has been available for a while now.

announcements.name: Three operational modes
announcements.shortDescription: Interactive (Copilot-style), reactive (alert-driven response via Azure Monitor, PagerDuty, ServiceNow), and proactive (scheduled cron-based health, compliance, and security checks)
announcements.longDescription: The Azure SRE Agent can be used in three ways designed to span the full operational lifecycle. Interactive mode lets you chat directly with the agent in the Azure portal, ask diagnostics questions, perform natural language operations, and upload task or HAR files for trace analysis—essentially a Copilot mode that assumes a human is driving. Reactive mode is the alert-driven response mode where the agent responds automatically to Azure Monitor alerts and integrates with PagerDuty and ServiceNow, performing automated triage, initial root cause analysis, and triggering mitigation with approval. Proactive mode runs autonomously on a schedule using cron expressions for continuous health and compliance checks, anomaly detection, security posture assessment, and resource optimization recommendations.

announcements.name: Enterprise trust and control layer
announcements.shortDescription: Built-in reader/standard/administrator roles, per-agent user-assigned managed identity, "on behalf of" elevation, review versus autonomous run modes, command validation hooks, and KQL-queryable audit trails in Application Insights
announcements.longDescription: The Azure SRE Agent builds trust and control into every layer across permissions, governance, security, and monitoring. There are three built-in user roles—reader, standard user, and administrator—each scoped to the persona's needs, and every agent gets its own user-assigned managed identity (so no secrets or API keys to manage) with an "on behalf of" (OBO) flow to temporarily elevate without standing access. Governance is controlled through run modes: review mode proposes actions and waits for administrator approval, while autonomous mode executes directly for trusted recurring tasks. It also supports command validation hooks that inspect and validate every command or tool call before execution, with every action logged to Application Insights as a full audit trail queryable with KQL.

announcements.name: Inbuilt evaluation metrics
announcements.shortDescription: An Intent Met quality score automatically calculated on every completed thread, rated on a one-to-five scale
announcements.longDescription: The Azure SRE Agent includes inbuilt evals such as the Intent Met quality score, which is automatically calculated on every completed thread and rated on a one-to-five scale so you can measure effectiveness over time. This sits alongside other monitoring capabilities including Session Insights for structured conversation summaries, an incident metrics dashboard showing mitigation rates and hours saved, and agent consumption tracking of Azure AI units used per day.
